senses.definition: (onomatopoeia) The sound of a quiet cough or of clearing one's throat.

examples: Ahem! Could we please get started?

quotes.text: Enter Nobody, and the Clowne. / Nobody. Ahem boy, Nobody is ſound yet for all his troubles.
quotes.reference: [1606], No-body, and Some-body. […], [London]: […] [James Roberts] for Iohn Trundle […], signature D2, verso:

examples: Ahem! In case you didn't notice, I did my share of the work, too.

senses.definition: Indicates the speaker does not wish to be perceived as rude, often intimating an impolite meaning to a third party that the speaker is not addressing.

subsenses.definition: Indicates subtle sarcasm, polite lying, or euphemism.
examples: I really (ahem!) liked the chocolate broccoli surprise.

quotes.text: The tone of Fat is casual and ahem, digestible, while also providing a succinct and significant overview of fatness and some of the issues most relevant to the burgeoning field of fat studies.
quotes.reference: 2020 December 15, Jenna M. Wilson, “Fat by Hanne Blank, Bloomsbury Academic, 2020”, in Fat Studies, volume 10, number 2, →DOI, pages 205–207:

senses.definition: To cough or clear one's throat so as to draw attention.

quotes.text: He wouldn't have been suspected of crying for the world, but he coughed and ahemmed, and finally turned away without speaking.
quotes.reference: 1856, Louise Chandler Moulton, Juno Clifford, page 108:

quotes.text: A full inspiration, preparatory to hawking, ahemming, or premeditated careful coughing, would excite an explosion of an unusually violent and persistent cough, hurrying the breath out of the poor victims.
